topic.title: Polar Function Graphs
topic.summary: Graphing r = f(θ) in polar coordinates: reading angle as direction and output as signed radius, connecting the rectangular graph of r against θ to the polar curve, and restricting the domain to draw part of a curve.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the graph of the polar function r = 3?
choices: A single point 3 units from the origin
A circle of radius 3 centered at the origin
questions.explanation: Every angle θ is paired with radius 3, so the graph is every point 3 units from the origin: a circle.
choiceExplanations: x = 3 is the rectangular graph; in polar coordinates r = 3 means distance 3 in every direction.
θ = 3 would fix the direction, not the distance.
Every value of θ gives a different point at distance 3.
All directions, distance 3.
questions.distinguisher: In r = 3, the distance is constant and the angle varies.

questions.prompt: For 0 ≤ θ < 2π, at which value of θ does the graph of r = 2 + 2 cos θ pass through the origin?
questions.explanation: The graph is at the origin when r = 0: 2 + 2 cos θ = 0 means cos θ = −1, so θ = π.
choiceExplanations: At θ = 0, r = 4, the point farthest from the origin.
At θ = π/2, r = 2.

questions.prompt: For the polar function r = 3 sin(2θ), the point with θ = 3π/4 lies in which quadrant?
questions.explanation: r = 3 sin(3π/2) = −3. The ray of 3π/4 points into Quadrant II, and a negative r places the point the opposite way, in Quadrant IV.
choiceExplanations: The ray of 3π/4 is in Quadrant II, but r is negative.
Quadrant I is not on the line through the ray of 3π/4.
Quadrant III is not on the line through the ray of 3π/4.
Negative r reverses the direction of the Quadrant II ray.
questions.distinguisher: Check the sign of r before choosing the quadrant.

questions.prompt: Which interval of θ draws exactly the petal of r = 3 sin(2θ) that lies in Quadrant I?
questions.explanation: r = 0 at θ = 0 and θ = π/2, and r > 0 between them, so 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2 starts and ends at the origin and stays in Quadrant I.
choiceExplanations: On π/2 < θ < π, r < 0, which adds a petal in Quadrant IV.
0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4 draws only half of the petal, out to r = 3.
The petal runs from r = 0 to r = 3 and back to r = 0.
This draws half of the Quadrant I petal and half of the Quadrant IV petal.

questions.prompt: What is the greatest distance from the origin of any point on the graph of r = 1 + 2 cos θ?
questions.explanation: The distance is |r|. r ranges from 1 + 2(1) = 3 at θ = 0 to 1 + 2(−1) = −1 at θ = π, so the greatest |r| is 3.
choiceExplanations: 1 is |r| at θ = π, the far point of the inner loop.
|r| is largest at θ = 0, where r = 3.
2 is the coefficient of cos θ.
−1 is the smallest value of r, and a distance is never negative.
questions.distinguisher: Distance is |r|, so check both the largest and smallest r.

questions.prompt: For π/2 < θ < π, the polar function r = 4 cos θ has negative values. In which quadrant are the points of the graph for these values of θ?
questions.explanation: The rays for π/2 < θ < π point into Quadrant II. Since r < 0, each point is placed the opposite way, in Quadrant IV.
choiceExplanations: Quadrant I is not opposite Quadrant II.
The rays are in Quadrant II, but negative r reverses the direction.
Quadrant III is not on the lines through these rays.
Opposite Quadrant II.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the graph of r = θ for θ ≥ 0?
choices: A straight line through the origin
A circle centered at the origin
A spiral that moves farther from the origin as θ increases
A spiral that moves closer to the origin as θ increases
questions.explanation: As θ increases, the direction keeps turning counterclockwise while the distance r = θ keeps growing, which traces an outward spiral.
choiceExplanations: r = θ is a line when graphed with θ and r as rectangular axes, but not in polar coordinates.
A circle needs a constant r.
Turning angle, growing radius.
r = θ increases, so the points move away from the origin.
questions.distinguisher: Don't confuse the r–θ graph with the polar graph.

questions.prompt: The graph of a polar function is shown. Which of the following could be its equation?

stimulusBlocks.caption: Graph of a polar function
stimulusBlocks.alt: A heart-shaped curve with its point at the origin. It extends 4 units up along the positive y-axis and 2 units left and right along the x-axis.

questions.explanation: The curve is farthest from the origin, 4 units, straight up at θ = π/2, and passes through the origin at θ = 3π/2. r = 2 + 2 sin θ gives r = 4 at π/2, r = 0 at 3π/2, and r = 2 at θ = 0 and π.
choiceExplanations: r = 2 + 2 cos θ is the same cardioid turned to point along the polar axis, with r = 4 at θ = 0.
r = 4 at π/2, 0 at 3π/2, and 2 at 0 and π.
r = 4 sin(2θ) is a four-petal rose.
r = 2 sin θ is a circle of diameter 2.
questions.distinguisher: The direction of the largest r tells you sine or cosine.

questions.prompt: Which interval of θ draws only the part of the graph of r = 2 + 2 cos θ that is on or above the x-axis?
questions.explanation: r = 2 + 2 cos θ ≥ 0 for every θ, so each point lies on its own terminal ray. The rays for 0 ≤ θ ≤ π are on or above the x-axis, and they trace the whole upper half from (4, 0) to the origin.
choiceExplanations: r is never negative, so the rays with 0 ≤ θ ≤ π give exactly the upper half.
−π/2 ≤ θ ≤ π/2 draws the right half of the curve, not the upper half.
π ≤ θ ≤ 2π draws the lower half.
0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2 stops at (2, π/2) and misses the upper-left part.
questions.distinguisher: When r ≥ 0, the points lie on the rays themselves.

questions.prompt: A student says the pair (θ, r) = (π/4, −2) cannot be on the graph of a polar function, because a radius cannot be negative. Which of the following is the best response?
choices: The student is correct, because a radius is a distance.
The student is correct, because polar functions are only defined for r ≥ 0.
The student is incorrect, because r is a signed displacement; r = −2 is opposite the ray of π/4.
The student is incorrect, because (π/4, −2) is the same point as (π/4, 2).
questions.explanation: Output values of a polar function are signed radial displacements. A negative r puts the point 2 units from the origin along the line of θ = π/4, in the opposite direction, in Quadrant III.
choiceExplanations: |r| is the distance; r itself carries a sign.
Polar functions such as r = 1 + 2 cos θ do take negative values.
Negative r means the opposite direction.
(π/4, 2) is in Quadrant I; (π/4, −2) is in Quadrant III.
questions.distinguisher: r is signed; |r| is the distance.
